content.text: : guanosine nucleoside analog that is highly potent for suppressing HBV DNA polymerase

: monotherapy is not recommended for patients coinfected with HIV and HBV since there is a greater potential for developing resistance to HIV antiretroviral agents; if coinfected, then entecavir should only be used if antiretroviral therapy (ART) is also being prescribed
: acyclic adenine nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor; inhibits both HIV (reverse transcriptase) and HBV (DNA polymerase activity) viral replication
: first line agent; indicated for HBeAg+ and HBeAg- CHB and HIV when prescribed with other ART
: nephrotoxicity, Fanconi’s syndrome, decreased BMD, osteomalacia
: synthetic guanosine analog that inhibits HCV polymerase; inhibits replications of RNA & DNA viruses
: HCV in combination w/ other agents (never as monotherapy)
: teratogenic, embryocidal – at least 2 forms of contraception must be used during therapy & for 6mo after tx
: HCV genotype 1 – treatment-naïve or treatment-experienced, w/ or w/o cirrhosis
•given as triple therapy w/ pegylated interferon & ribavirin
: rash, itching, photosensitivity reactions (pts should limit sun exposure & use sunscreens)
: HCV genotypes 1-4; CANNOT BE TAKEN AS MONOTHERAPY
•should be used in combination w/ ribavirin for tx of chronic HCV in pts w/ hepatocellular carcinoma awaiting liver transplantation for up to 48wks or until transplantation, whichever is first
: NS5A replication complex inhibitor + NS5B polymerase inhibitor
: HCV genotypes 1 or 4; use in children ≥3yo or those weighing ≥35kg for genotypes 1, 4, 5, or 6
: NS5B polymerase inhibitor + NS5A replication complex inhibitor
: recommended for use in all 6 HCV genotypes; indicated for treatment-naïve & treatment-experienced pts w/ class A cirrhosis or w/o cirrhosis
: NS5B inhibitor + NS5A inhibitor + NS3/4A protease inhibitor
: reserved for pts who have failed prior DAA therapies; 95% effective for all 6 genotypes
: NS5A replication complex inhibitor + NS3/4A protease inhibitor
: approved for HCV genotypes 1 & 4; in treatment-naïve or treatment-experienced pts w/ or w/o cirrhosis
•recommended for use in renal insufficiency including hemodialysis
: mod-severe hepatic disease, strong 3A4 inducers, & efavirenz
: NS3/4A protease inhibitor + NS5A replication complex inhibitor
: approved for all 6 HCV genotypes in pts who have failed prior DAA therapy
•recommended for use in renal insufficiency including hemodialysis
: efavirenz, cyclosporine, and concurrent ethinyl estradiol products including hormone replacement and oral contraceptives due to a potential for ALT increases
